Chooses ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B before all origins o, finite domains Λ, cuts A and natural C,k₀; under 2 <= C and 50000000 <= k₀, retains actual sparse residue functions, every coefficient-64 cell estimate, finite support, exact finite M membership and its boundary bound. Supplies S : M → ℝ with positive values, an actual incident selected cell at some k >= k₀ witnessing S v = 2^(fineScaleIndex k), and S v <= 2^(fineScaleIndex h) for every selected incident cell at h >= k₀. For distinct v,w : M it proves max (S v) (S w) / 4 <= dist v.val w.val. The minimum side is exact, although its layer index need not be unique.

For arbitrary origin o, natural indices k,h >= 50000000, finite endpoint set Z and natural C >= 2, let z and w belong to fineLayerIndices o k (fineScaleIndex k) Z C and fineLayerIndices o h (fineScaleIndex h) Z C. For distinct actual cell marks x ∈ beltCellMarks o (fineScaleIndex k) z and y ∈ beltCellMarks o (fineScaleIndex h) w, proves max (2^(fineScaleIndex k)) (2^(fineScaleIndex h)) / 4 <= dist x y. This applies to every actual fine-layer cell, and hence to selected belt cells; it imposes no endpoint-set nonemptiness or fan hypothesis.
